A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SoftVQ-VAE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction and generation experiments, representation analyses, and tokenizer ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds auxiliary-loss tests, codeword visualizations, and further TiTok comparisons including COCO reconstruction.

M1.justification: The architecture, soft categorical posterior, representation alignment and training objective remain unchanged, as do the GMMVQ, product-quantization and residual-quantization variants. Newly tested codebook and commitment losses are ablation variants.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 and Table 10 add MSCOCO reconstruction evaluation to the existing ImageNet coverage. ImageNet reconstruction, conditional generation and linear-probing tasks remain.

E2.justification: The original comparisons are retained. New Table 10 expands the TiTok comparison with TiTok-B-64, TiTok-L-32 and TiTok-LL-KL-32 alongside the previously evaluated BL-KL and BL-VQ variants.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces separate SoftVQ-S-64 controls adding codebook or commitment loss, and Table 10 evaluates additional TiTok configurations. Existing training budgets, metrics and guidance settings are unchanged. The new COCO split and sample count are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds tests of whether codebook and commitment losses help, plus a visualization comparing codeword coverage in VQ and SoftVQ. These supplement the retained alignment, quantization, codebook-size, latent-size and temperature analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original tables retain their numerical entries. New Table 5 reports gFID 13.35 for SoftVQ-S-64, 15.15 with codebook loss and 14.35 with commitment loss; Table 10 adds reconstruction, probing and generation results. Its TiTok-BL-VQ rFID of 2.60 differs from the retained Table 3 value of 2.06 without an explained setting difference, so this is an unresolved additional report.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), including the posterior and KL derivations and quantization formulations, are retained. The new gradient-flow discussion supplies an informal explanation rather than a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about continuous tokenization, 32/64-token compression, semantic representations and generation efficiency. Their headline performance and speedup claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 expands the explanation of how indirect codebook updates hinder representation alignment in VQ and interprets SoftVQ's codeword coverage. Appendix D.3 explicitly qualifies the TiTok comparison by noting different training arrangements despite similar architectures.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 newly specifies TiTok's two-stage decoding with a pretrained tokenizer when contrasting it with SoftVQ's single-decoder, end-to-end training. Appendix C's implementation settings, hardware disclosures and the code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix D.3 explicitly acknowledges that soft assignment is an existing idea and positions the claimed novelty in highly compressed continuous tokenization. It also sharpens the distinction from TiTok. The cited-work set remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording corrections and sentence cuts, adds Appendices A.1 and D.3, and renames the reconstruction and generation visualization subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5 and 10 and the codeword visualization in Figure 5. Existing displays are retained with local formatting, reflow and renumbering; Table 10 appears on a separate final page after the image galleries.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, the new loss ablations and expanded TiTok/COCO comparisons provide useful additional support for the design and reconstruction capabilities. The benefit is limited by sparse details for the added experiments and unexplained discrepancies, including TiTok-BL-VQ rFID 2.06 in Table 3 versus 2.60 in Table 10. These additions modestly strengthen the paper while leaving its core method and main evidence unchanged.
